राउरकेला में झमाझम बारिश, छह जिलों में रेड अलर्ट
- कॉपी लिंक
भास्कर न्यूज | राउरकेला
ओडिशा में चक्रवात ‘अर्नब’ का प्रभाव अब कई इलाकों में दिखाई देने लगा है। आंध्र प्रदेश के काकीनाडा तट के पास चक्रवात के लैंडफॉल के बाद राज्य के विभिन्न जिलों में बारिश का दौर जारी है। दक्षिण ओडिशा के गजपति, मलकानगिरि, कोरापुट और रायगढ़ा जिलों में भारी बारिश हुई। वहीं, राजधानी भुवनेश्वर के अलावा पुरी और कटक में भी बारिश दर्ज की गई है। मौसम में आए बदलाव से लोगों की परेशानी बढ़ने की आशंका है।
चक्रवात का असर पश्चिमी ओडिशा तक पहुंचने लगा है। इस्पात नगरी राउरकेला में बुधवार सुबह से आसमान में बादल छाए हुए हैं और रुक-रुककर बूंदाबांदी हो रही है। सुंदरगढ़ जिले के अन्य इलाकों में भी हल्की बारिश जारी है। अचानक बदले मौसम से दैनिक कामकाज और आवागमन प्रभावित होने की आशंका जताई जा रही है। मौसम संबंधी उपलब्ध जानकारी के अनुसार, गुरुवार को राउरकेला और आसपास के क्षेत्रों में बारिश की तीव्रता बढ़ सकती है। ऐसे में निचले इलाकों, जलभराव की आशंका वाले स्थानों और प्रमुख सड़कों पर विशेष सतर्कता बरतने की जरूरत है।
चक्रवात के संभावित प्रभाव को देखते हुए ओडिशा के छह जिलों में रेड अलर्ट जारी किए जाने की जानकारी है। कई अन्य जिलों में भी भारी बारिश को लेकर चेतावनी दी गई है। प्रशासन मौसम की स्थिति पर लगातार नजर रख रहा है। प्रतिकूल मौसम की आशंका के बीच नागरिकों से अपील की गई है कि वे मौसम विभाग और जिला प्रशासन की आधिकारिक सलाह का पालन करें। अनावश्यक यात्रा से बचें और तेज बारिश के दौरान सुरक्षित स्थानों पर रहें। फिलहाल, आने वाले दिनों में बारिश की तीव्रता और चक्रवात के प्रभाव पर सभी की नजर बनी हुई है।

बंगाल की खाड़ी में चक्रवाती तूफान का खतरा, पूर्वी तट के राज्यों में अलर्ट; 19 नवंबर से भारी बारिश की चेतावनी
बंगाल की खाड़ी में बन रहा गहरा दबाव तेजी से मजबूत हो रहा है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) के अनुसार, इसके सोमवार शाम तक चक्रवाती तूफान में बदलने की संभावना है। इस संभावित तूफान को ‘अकवान’ (Akvan) नाम दिया गया है। मौसम विभाग ने आशंका जताई है कि 17 नवंबर तक यह भीषण चक्रवाती तूफान और 19 नवंबर तक बहुत भीषण चक्रवाती तूफान का रूप ले सकता है। इसके संभावित प्रभाव को देखते हुए ओडिशा समेत पूर्वी तट के राज्यों में सतर्कता बढ़ा दी गई है।
Cyclone Akvan: कहां पहुंचा तूफान का सिस्टम?
IMD के मुताबिक, बंगाल की खाड़ी में बना गहरा दबाव पिछले छह घंटों में उत्तर-पश्चिम दिशा की ओर 8 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से आगे बढ़ा है। फिलहाल यह विशाखापत्तनम से लगभग 870 किलोमीटर और गोपालपुर से करीब 980 किलोमीटर दक्षिण-दक्षिणपूर्व में स्थित है। इसके आंध्र प्रदेश के तट की ओर बढ़ने की संभावना जताई गई है।
Odisha Weather Alert: 16 जिलों में येलो अलर्ट
संभावित चक्रवाती तूफान के प्रभाव से ओडिशा में 18 नवंबर से मौसम बदल सकता है। मौसम विभाग ने 16 जिलों में येलो अलर्ट जारी किया है। वहीं, 19 से 21 नवंबर के बीच राज्य के कई हिस्सों में भारी बारिश और तेज हवाएं चलने की आशंका है।
इन जिलों में ऑरेंज अलर्ट, भारी बारिश की चेतावनी
- 19 नवंबर: पुरी, गंजाम और गजपति में भारी बारिश का ऑरेंज अलर्ट।
- 20 नवंबर: गंजाम, गजपति, रायगढ़ा, कोरापुट और मलकानगिरी में ऑरेंज अलर्ट।
- 21 नवंबर: बरगढ़, झारसुगुड़ा और सुंदरगढ़ में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी।
Delhi AQI: दिल्ली में प्रदूषण भी बढ़ा
दूसरी ओर, दिल्ली-NCR में वायु प्रदूषण की स्थिति चिंताजनक बनी हुई है। सोमवार सुबह दिल्ली का औसत AQI 216 दर्ज किया गया, जबकि सिरी फोर्ट में यह 346 तक पहुंच गया। वहीं, AQI.in के अमेरिकी AQI स्केल के अनुसार दिल्ली का AQI 800 बताया गया है। अलग-अलग AQI स्केल के कारण इन आंकड़ों में अंतर हो सकता है।

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) again dropped more than 50% from its peak in November 2026. The price fell as low as $62,438, down 50.6% from its all-time high of $126,296 reached in October 2025. Despite this decline, Bitcoin remains up approximately 8,300% over the last decade.
Investors in the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust (NYSEARCA: BTC), which the SEC registered as a spot Bitcoin ETF, are experiencing similar downturns. However, Bitcoin has crossed the 50% threshold in previous cycles. So, what has Bitcoin done each time it fell 50% from its all-time high?
Bitcoin Fell Below Half Its All-Time High Again in November
Since hitting its low, Bitcoin has rebounded to $64,664, 48.8% below its all-time high and 2.4% above the halfway mark of $63,148. The low was the deepest since August, coinciding with a 14.9% weekly loss and a 20.8% loss over the past 30 days, as detailed in “Why Bitcoin Is Declining.”
According to Bianco Research, Bitcoin peaked for this move on September 21 and has since fallen over 25%. Binance Research noted that the 15.6% drop over the 11 days to November 14 was Bitcoin’s sharpest sell-off over a stretch that long.
Data from Glassnode indicates that the largest cluster of holder costs, or the price at which most coins last changed hands, lies between $60,000 and $63,000. This means a significant number of holders are around this breakeven point, which we explored in what happens if Bitcoin drops below $65,000.
Michael Saylor, chairman of Strategy, hinted at potential buying on November 15, posting, “This dip could use a little orange” on X.
Every Earlier 50% Fall Ended in a New All-Time High
In every previous cycle, Bitcoin kept falling after crossing the 50% mark, sometimes for more than a year.

The drop in 2021 was the quickest recovery, with Bitcoin reaching a new all-time high in October 2021, five months after crossing the 50% mark. However, after hitting that high, it closed November 2021 at $57,030, and by May 2022, it had fallen to $31,853 as the next bear market began.
Full bear markets have historically taken longer to recover. Bitcoin fell after crossing the 50% mark in January 2018, hitting a low of $5,830 by June 2018. After crossing in January 2022, it closed at $23,314 in July 2022 and $23,153 in January 2023, even briefly rebounding to $48,130 in March 2022 before falling below the line again.
Even so, every complete cycle ended with a new all-time high. Bitcoin surpassed its 2011 peak by April 2013, its 2013 peak by March 2017, its 2017 peak by December 2020, and its 2021 peak by March 2024.
The 2026 Fall Is Shallower So Far, and Spot ETFs Are New
Bitcoin already crossed the 50% threshold once this cycle, dropping to $60,001 in February, bottoming at $57,718 in July, and closing August at $78,563, six months after the first crossing. The November decline marks a second drop for the current cycle, similar to 2022 when Bitcoin rebounded above the threshold in March before falling again.
So far, this decline is shallower. The deepest 2026 drop, 54.3%, is closer to the 55.4% drop of 2021 than the deeper declines of 77.3% to 93.1% seen in full bear markets. Additionally, this is the first cycle with spot Bitcoin ETFs in brokerage accounts, which began trading in January 2024.
A guest on the Unchained podcast argued on October 30 that the buyers who drove Bitcoin’s price from $58,000 to $80,000 in August were “longer-term people with longer-term views on Bitcoin” who are less likely to sell during short-term market turbulence. The guest added that “everything historically looks like Bitcoin’s bottom is in,” while conceding the call could be wrong.
The November drop now seriously tests that belief. It also highlights a fundamental question in any market bubble: who gets to keep the gains. Our free Bubble Survivor’s Handbook covers strategies for riding out manias and planning an exit.
Bitcoin Recovered From Every 50% Fall After First Falling Further
Every time Bitcoin fell 50% below its all-time high, it kept declining for 1 to 13 months before setting a new all-time high. The challenge remains waiting for recovery. Over the last five years, Bitcoin has risen only 3.4%, showing how long a full recovery can take.
So far in 2026, the decline looks more like the shallow dip in 2021 than the severe bear markets. If the holder cost cluster between $60,000 and $63,000 holds, Bitcoin could repeat the 2021 rebound. However, if that level breaks, Bitcoin could revisit the July low of $57,718, 10.7% below the current price.
Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most. Snow warning: Met Office issues yellow alert in Lancashire starting at midnight
Snow is on the way in parts of Lancashire - the first of the winter season.
Skip to main contentSnow warning: Met Office issues yellow alert in Lancashire starting at midnight
Lancashire may be in for some snow tonight and tomorrow as the Met Office issues a weather warning across the county.
A yellow snow alert, stretching from Staffordshire in the West Midlands to south-west Scotland, will be in force from 12am until 11am on Tuesday.
Some roads and railways are likely to be affected, and there is a “small chance” of power outages and an impact on mobile phone service, the Met Office said.
The affected area covers much of Yorkshire, as well as Derbyshire, Northumberland, Greater Manchester, Cumbria and Lancashire.
Meanwhile, the AA is advising drivers to get prepared with the Met Office warning that snow could make journeys difficult across parts of Britain on Tuesday morning (17 November).
Forecasters said a band of rain is expected to head northwards across the UK through Monday night and Tuesday morning which will likely turn to snow after it encounters colder air in the warning area.
Locations at 100-metre altitude or higher will mainly be affected, with any snow falling below this level likely to be temporary and quickly melting, the Met Office said.
In areas where snow does accumulate, depths of 1-5cm are likely with some locations above 300-400 metres potentially seeing 5-15 cm, it added.
Met Office chief forecaster Dan Suri said: “The greatest chance of settling snow will be over ground above 200 metres, with 1-5 cm possible in places and potentially 5-15 cm above 300-400 metres.
“Combined with strong easterly winds, this could bring some travel disruption to higher-level routes.
“Through Tuesday morning the snow will increasingly turn back to rain, with some minor surface-water impacts also possible.
“Away from higher ground, and so for many people, rain rather than snow will be the main story, although it will continue to feel cold in the north.
“Temperatures will be closer to average further south, before more settled conditions gradually develop here late this week.”
It comes after the UK saw its coldest night of the season so far on Sunday, with a low of minus 7.7C recorded at Tulloch Bridge in the Scottish Highlands.
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued a yellow cold health alert for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber, in place until 9am on Thursday.
These alerts mean weather conditions could result in an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life for vulnerable people, the agency said.
Lee Morley, AA expert patrol, said: "The first snowfall of the season can catch drivers out, particularly when we've become used to milder conditions. Even if snow doesn't settle where you live, temperatures can still fall low enough for frost and ice to make roads slippery.
"One of the simplest things drivers can do is prepare their vehicle before the cold weather arrives. Check your screenwash is suitable for winter, make sure your tyres are in good condition and allow enough time to completely clear your windscreen before setting off. A quick check now could save you from a breakdown or a difficult journey later.
"If you're heading out in snow or icy conditions, reduce your speed, leave a much bigger gap to the vehicle in front and avoid harsh braking or sudden steering movements. Take particular care on bridges, exposed roads and shaded areas where ice can remain even when other roads appear clear. If conditions are particularly bad, consider whether your journey is essential."
